- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.40) and forecast shows a sharp downward spike, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to peak value.
- If sentiment is positive (especially > 0.20) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, model tends to overshoot — cap upward movement at 10–15% above recent high.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) — add 2–3% to forecast for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- Model overestimates true price in late 30-day horizon (last 5–7 days) — reduce forecast by 2–5% if sentiment is negative or volatile.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to lag — delay downward correction by 1–2 days and reduce slope of decline.
- If sentiment history shows repeated positive swings (e.g., 3+ consecutive positive values), model tends to overreact — dampen upward momentum by 5–10% in forecast.
- Model often fails to capture mean reversion after sharp spikes — if price spiked >10% above 14-day moving average, reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently negative and price is trending down, model tends to underestimate — add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–5 days to account for sentiment-driven support.
